institution: Regional Institute of Medical Sciences, Imphal
citation: Regional Institute of Medical Sciences Hospital, Imphal. RIMSH Antibiogram 2023-24 (1 July 2023 to 30 June 2024). Imphal: RIMS.
reporting: Percent susceptible with isolate numbers: Enterobacterales by specimen (blood, urine, lower respiratory tract, superficial infection); S. aureus (MSSA, MRSA) and CoNS from all samples, with CoNS species; A. baumannii and P. aeruginosa by specimen and by location (OPD, ward, ICU); E. faecalis and E. faecium by specimen and by location.
method: Isolate data entered monthly on the AMR portal, validated by the regional administrator and analysed with the iAMRSN portal; the staphylococcal, non-fermenter and enterococcal tables leave groups under 20 isolates unanalysed ('-').

verification.note: Read from page images (scanned PDF, no text layer). Every table was read twice from separately rendered and cropped images (pass A at scale 3, pass B at scale 2.5 with different crops) and only values both passes agreed on were kept; isolate numbers were checked against the count tables (Tables 1.2 and 1.3, p14, p19) and every location table's Total column against its OPD, ward and ICU columns weighted by their isolate numbers. Page numbers are PDF pages. Checked 2026-09-26.

notes: RIMSH Antibiogram 2023-24 (the file name says 2023; the analysis period is 1 July 2023 to 30 June 2024): 18,917 samples and 6,407 culture-positive isolates. Enterobacterales tables are by specimen for all locations; the A. baumannii, P. aeruginosa and enterococcal location tables cover all specimens except faeces (recorded as all specimens). There is no sterile-site antibiogram; the SS count column is recorded as sterile sites, as the 2026 policy defines SS (fluid from sterile spaces), although this report's text calls SS surgical sites. The report prints 0 for agents not tested in its trend tables, so a 0 in rows with few isolates may mean not tested; values are recorded as printed. Cefazolin is 0 for every organism in the blood table. 'Staphylococcus spp.' in the CoNS table is recorded as other (unspeciated) coagulase-negative staphylococci; the CoNS table prints one isolate fewer for each species than the distribution table (p14). The faeces table (p5) lists 183 diarrhoeagenic E. coli, while Tables 1.2 and 1.3 count 162 as diarrhoeagenic E. coli and 21 as E. coli, so Table 1.2's E. coli total (2,001) includes 21 faecal isolates. Gentamicin HL is high-level gentamicin.
issues: Second reader 2026-09-26: the PDF has no text layer but is not a raster scan: every page is vector outlines, so renders at scale 3 to 4 are sharp. All 809 cells, all 78 row n and all 110 counts re-read from those renders and written down before comparing (this includes the seeded sample of 202 cells over all 13 tables): 0 corrected. Organism, specimen, setting, phenotype and page agree for all 78 rows; the rotated Table 1.3 (p8) was read turned upright.

Second reader: all 58 cells the validator does not keep (31 cautions, 27 intrinsic) are printed as recorded, including E. coli imipenem 27.8 (blood) and 35.8 (urine) against meropenem 55.6 and 64.4, and E. faecalis vancomycin 100 in the p24 Total column against 97.7 in its ward column (conflict entry kept).

Second reader: the 7 count mismatches are printed that way: Table 1.3 (p8) prints 10 superficial-infection Enterobacter spp. against 11 in the p11 table; Table 1.2 (p7) prints P. aeruginosa 439 (OPD 94) and E. faecium 196 (ward 123) against 438 (93) on p19 and p21 and 195 (122) on p24; p14 prints Staphylococcus spp. 93 and S. epidermidis 50 against 92 and 49 on p17.
